title: Compound V job_result
description: Canonical, backend-independent result of one dispatched job. Identical shape across the claude, codex, and antigravity adapters. The enforcement fields (blocked, files_changed, violations) are GIT-DERIVED by the caller, never self-reported by the worker model; the model's --output-last-message text feeds only `summary`. Also usable as a codex `--output-schema` target.

status.description: Terminal disposition of the job. `blocked` means a scope violation; `timeout` means the timeout wrapper fired; `error` is any other non-zero exit.

blocked.description: True if any file outside write_allowed changed. Git-derived by the scope gate, never model-self-reported. When true, status MUST be `blocked` and the caller MUST NOT merge.

files_changed.description: Repo-relative paths the job actually changed: `git diff --name-only` UNION `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` inside the worktree (or against the baseline commit for direct jobs).

violations.description: Subset of files_changed that fall outside write_allowed. Non-empty ⇒ blocked. Git-derived.

summary.description: Human-readable one-paragraph summary. Sourced from --output-last-message (or the schema'd JSON) — informational only, never used for enforcement.

session_id.description: Backend session/run identifier for resume. For codex: the UUID captured from the first `--json` `thread.started` event's `thread_id` (UUID-validated), resumed via `codex exec resume <uuid>` only under the resume-eligibility rule. Empty string when the backend has no resumable session.

worktree.description: Absolute path of the worktree the job ran in, or empty string for `direct` (in-place) jobs. Worktrees live under $TMPDIR/compound-v/<run-id>/<job-id>.

exit_code.description: Raw process exit code of the worker (0 on success; 124 if the timeout wrapper fired).

failure_class.description: On a non-success status, the classified backend-failure reason from compound-v-classify-failure.py (out_of_credits | rate_limited | overloaded | auth | context_length | timeout | network | other). null on success/blocked. Drives the dispatcher's deterministic retry/reroute/halt policy (compound-v-failure-policy.py): out_of_credits/auth never retry; out_of_credits circuit-breaks the backend and re-routes remaining jobs to the fallback; transient classes retry with capped backoff.

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds-until-retry parsed from the provider message (HTTP Retry-After, or a codex usage-limit countdown like 'try again in 5 days'), 0 when unknown. The dispatcher passes this to compound-v-failure-policy.py --retry-after so a retry honors the provider's stated wait instead of synthetic backoff.

tests.description: OPTIONAL, MEASURED-ONLY record of the test contract this job actually ran (v3.0 Feature B3). The resolved contract reaches a worker as a REAL ARGUMENT (--test-contract-file), never as prose inside the prompt, and the values here are produced by the WORKER that ran the commands — never self-reported by the executor model, the same rule that governs blocked/files_changed/violations. Omitted entirely when the job ran no tests (no contract passed, or the job was blocked/timed out/errored and never reached the test step): absent is honest, an invented zero is not. Tests run AFTER the git-derived scope gate, so a file a test writes into the worktree can never become a false violation — and, for the same reason, anything a test creates after the gate is outside the gate's authority and MUST NOT be merged (see skills/backend-launcher/SKILL.md, Merge-back).

command.description: The test command(s) this job ACTUALLY executed, in execution order, newline-separated when the resolved set held more than one. Never a plan or an intention — only what ran. The review gate reads this field, and a job that reports no test command at all is a FAIL (Feature B4), which is why it is required whenever this object is present.

exit_code.description: 0 iff EVERY executed command exited 0; otherwise the exit code of the FIRST command that failed (124 when the process-group timeout supervisor fired). Commands are not short-circuited — every resolved command runs, so `failures` is complete even when an early one fails. A non-zero value is merge-blocking for the caller: the worker only observes and reports, it never merges.

scope.description: The job's resolved `test_scope` (execution-manifest.md, Feature B2), copied verbatim from the contract the caller passed as an argument. `floor_only` means ONLY the floor, never nothing; a changed path matching no `when` glob resolves to `full_command` at tier FULL and, since 3.4.1, to the referencing tests (label `impacted+referencing`, cap 5) or the floor alone at SCOPED/DIRECT — so an unmapped file is never silently untested, and never the whole suite at a proportionate tier.

selected_count.description: How many resolved COMMANDS this run executed — a count of selected commands, not of individual test cases. No bundled worker parses an arbitrary runner's output, and reporting a case count it never read would be fabrication. A producer that does read a machine-readable report MAY report selected test cases instead, and must say so in `command`/`failures` granularity terms.

duration_ms.description: MEASURED-ONLY total wall-clock milliseconds around the supervised test invocations (it therefore includes the supervisor's own start-up, which is what running a test through this worker actually costs). ABSENT — never estimated, never zero-filled — when the runner or the worker could not measure it. It exists so a later release can say from our OWN data whether scoping saved time; a selected_count with no duration cannot answer that.

failures.description: MEASURED-ONLY machine-readable identifiers of the units that FAILED. The bundled workers report the exact failing command strings — command granularity is the finest identifier they can observe without parsing an arbitrary runner's output, and it is directly re-runnable. A producer that can read a machine-readable report (JUnit XML, pytest --json) SHOULD report per-test ids instead. An EMPTY array means measured-and-nothing-failed; the field is ABSENT when the runner reported nothing machine-readable, and B2's rule then applies: the next run's floor falls back to `full_command` rather than silently dropping the previously-failing set. Without this field "previously failing" is uncomputable, and the three-set floor silently degrades to two.

gate_receipt.description: Recovery semantics, matching scripts/compound-v-integration-gate.py exactly: MISSING or PARTIAL receipt => the verification layer re-derives from git and the derived verdict wins. COMPLETE but binding-mismatched => REFUSED OUTRIGHT as forged, never re-derived, because re-deriving a forgery over a tree that happens to be clean would reward it with a pass. An earlier wording promised re-derivation for the mismatched case; the code never did that, and the code is right.

baseline_commit.description: Full commit hash the job's diff was measured AGAINST — the SHA captured BEFORE `git worktree add` (or the recorded pre-dispatch commit for a direct job), never the literal "HEAD". Pinning the SHA is what makes an executor that COMMITS inside its worktree still visible to the gate.

realised_commit.description: Full commit hash of the tree the gate actually observed as this job's realised state (the worktree's HEAD at gate time). Equal to baseline_commit when the worker did not commit inside its worktree, which is the normal case.

diff_digest.description: Content address of the job's realised diff, as `<alg>:<hex>`. PINNED DEFAULT RECIPE, so a producer and the verification layer cannot diverge: `git -C <gate-root> add -A` (which brings untracked files — the half a plain `git diff` would miss — into the index), then sha256 over the raw bytes of `git -C <gate-root> diff --cached --binary <baseline_commit>`, rendered as `sha256:<64-hex>`. A producer using any other recipe MUST be able to say so, because a digest the verification layer cannot recompute is treated exactly like a missing one: the gate is re-run.

verdict.description: The gate's own verdict field, copied verbatim from its JSON output. `error` is a gate/environment fault and is NOT a pass — it fails closed, exactly as null does.

raw_stdout.description: The gate's literal stdout (its JSON verdict document) kept verbatim as evidence. Never a paraphrase or a model's account of it: the receipt is only worth as much as the raw text behind it, and re-deriving from a summary is the fabricated-evidence pattern.

exit_code.description: Raw exit code of the scope-gate process: 0 = pass, 1 = blocked, 2 = usage/git fault. A value the receipt's producer could not observe makes the receipt incomplete, and an incomplete receipt is a missing one.

usage.description: OPTIONAL, INFORMATIONAL, MEASURED-ONLY token accounting for this job. Worker-sourced like `summary`, NEVER fabricated and NEVER used for enforcement. TWO sources, both produced by compound-v-usage-extract.py and distinguished by `source`: (1) `backend-events` — the external backend's own structured usage events (codex/opencode/cursor); (2) `workflow-transcript` — for an Engine C job, the Claude Code subagent transcripts of that job's stages, deduplicated by message id (v3.4.17; a Claude worker writes no events log, which is why an Engine C result carried no usage at all before). When neither source exists (agy/antigravity, or a claude job whose transcripts were not scanned) `measured` is false and the token counts are null (anti-ruflo: a null is honest, a made-up number is not). Omitted entirely when no usage object was produced.

input_tokens.description: Total input/prompt tokens consumed by the job, summed across the backend's usage events (or across the job's transcript messages). null when not measured.

output_tokens.description: Total output/completion tokens produced by the job, summed across the backend's usage events (or across the job's transcript messages). null when not measured.

cache_read_input_tokens.description: OPTIONAL. Prompt-cache READ tokens, summed the same way. Emitted by the `workflow-transcript` source, where the harness reports it per assistant message; null or absent when the source does not report it. Separate from input_tokens on purpose — folding cached reads into the input total would misstate both.

cache_creation_input_tokens.description: OPTIONAL. Prompt-cache WRITE (creation) tokens, summed the same way. Emitted by the `workflow-transcript` source; null or absent when the source does not report it.

backend.description: Backend name this usage was extracted for (codex | opencode | cursor | agy | antigravity | claude).

measured.description: True only when real token counts were read from a real record — the backend's structured usage events, or the job's own subagent transcripts. False when no such record exists or it was absent/empty/unparseable; in that case the token counts are null.

source.description: OPTIONAL. Which record the numbers were read from: `backend-events` = the external backend's own structured events log; `workflow-transcript` = the Claude Code subagent transcripts of this job's Engine C stages. Absent on results written before v3.4.17, which are all backend-events.

transcripts.description: OPTIONAL, `workflow-transcript` source only. Basenames of the agent-*.jsonl transcripts that were summed for this job — normally its implement, gate and record stages. It is the evidence trail: a total whose transcripts cannot be named is a number nobody can re-derive.

retries.description: v3.4.8: every in-workflow retry of this job's stages — {stage, job, attempt, wait_ms} plus escalated_from/model on the reviewer lift. wait_ms is the wait that was REQUESTED (a workflow script cannot read a clock); Record stamps its own time when it writes the result.

escalated_from.description: v3.4.8: the MODEL rung a review job was lifted from (e.g. `opus`) when its retry budget was exhausted transiently — the REQUESTED escalation, never a confirmed outcome (an org allowlist can substitute silently). null when no lift happened.
